subject: Order Form: invoicing cadence, taxes & minimum commitment
messages:
From: Daniel Lee <daniel.lee@acme-analytics.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-05T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Order Form redlines + invoicing questions

Vanessa —

Thanks for sending the draft Order Form. Procurement reviewed and returned a redlined PDF (attached). A few quick items we want to confirm before routing to legal here:

- Invoicing cadence: procurement prefers monthly invoices, but they want invoices aligned to calendar month. Can Redwood support month-end invoicing?
- Net terms: they asked for net-60. Is that something we can accommodate?
- Taxes: they flagged the tax section; they are a registered entity in CA and will provide tax-exempt documentation if needed, but need clarity on whether Redwood will gross-up or withhold where applicable.
- Minimum commitment: the Order Form shows $100,000 annual minimum; they are asking whether that can be reduced to $75,000 given staging usage.

I've attached Acme's annotated redlines (Acme_OrderForm_Redlines.pdf). Happy to jump on a quick call if helpful.

Thanks,
Daniel
Procurement Manager
Acme Analytics

Attachment: Acme_OrderForm_Redlines.pdf (application/pdf)

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Lee <daniel.lee@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-05T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Order Form redlines + invoicing questions

Daniel —

Appreciate the detailed pass and the annotated PDF. Quick responses inline:

- Month-end invoicing: yes, we can align invoices to calendar month close. We typically issue invoices within 5 business days of month-end.
- Net-60: that is outside our standard net-30, so I will need to confirm with Finance. Can you share whether Acme has payment terms precedent with other vendors at net-60 (helps expedite)?
- Taxes: please send the tax exemption certificate if applicable. We need the legal name and tax ID to validate. We do not automatically gross-up; we handle tax the way the tax clause defines (customer responsibility for withholding unless otherwise noted).
- Minimum commit: thanks for flagging $75k. Internally I'll propose a compromise to Finance and Commercials (see below).

I attached a proposed payment schedule (redwood_proposed_schedule.xlsx) showing monthly invoices by calendar month and two pricing rows: standard and a 7% prepay discount if Acme elects annual prepay.

Next steps: 1) Can you confirm Acme's tax status and provide PO requirements (invoice address/PO number fields)? 2) If you're open, I can propose $90k minimum with quarterly invoicing and net-45 as a middle ground while we work with Finance.

If you prefer a quick 20-minute sync, I'm available tomorrow at 10:30am PT.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Account Exec | Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0122

Attachment: redwood_proposed_schedule.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, aisha_rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-06T08:45:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Order Form redlines + invoicing questions

Forwarding for visibility — adding Legal (Aisha) to help review the tax and MSA redlines. A few bullets for Commercials/Finance to consider:

- We should avoid gross-up language unless Acme can demonstrate withholding is required. If they are tax-exempt, require certificate up front.
- Net-45 compromise looks reasonable; net-60 is atypical for new logos without credit.
- Minimum commit: can we offer a temporary ramp schedule (e.g., $50k for first 6 months, then true-up to annual $90k) if Acme is uncomfortable committing to $90k immediately? This helps close the deal while protecting ARR.

Aisha — can you confirm the suggested language re: invoicing address, VAT vs sales tax, and whether we need an explicit tax indemnity clause?

-Ben
Director, Sales Operations

Subject: Re: Order Form redlines + invoicing questions

Ben / Vanessa —

Thanks for the quick responses. A few clarifications from our side:

- Tax status: Acme is registered for sales & use tax in CA but is not tax-exempt. I've attached our company tax certificate and vendor profile.
- PO requirements: procurement requires the invoice to include a PO number and remittance address (Acme Corp, Attn: Accounts Payable, 123 Commerce Way, Palo Alto, CA 94301).
- Minimum commit: we can go to $85k but cannot commit to $90k. We'd consider annual prepay if the discount moves to 10% (from your 7%).

I've attached the tax cert (acme_tax_cert.pdf). We can do a call on Monday to finalize the language.

Regards,
Daniel

Attachment: acme_tax_cert.pdf (application/pdf)

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Lee <daniel.lee@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, aisha_rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-09T10:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Order Form redlines + invoicing questions

Daniel —

Thanks for the tax cert and PO details — that's helpful. Proposed commercial compromise below:

- Minimum commitment: $85,000 annual (meets you in the middle).
- Invoicing cadence: monthly, aligned to calendar month; invoices issued within 5 business days of month-end.
- Net terms: net-45 standard. For net-60 we can consider on a case-by-case basis after two on-time payments; otherwise net-45 will apply.
- Prepay discount: 8% for annual prepay (split difference).
- Taxes: customer is responsible for sales & use tax as applicable; Redwood will not gross-up. Redwood will provide tax detail on each invoice and accept PO number/Remit-to as provided.

I've attached our redlined Order Form v3 (orderform_v3_redlines.pdf) with the proposed language for minimums, invoicing, and tax clause. Aisha — could you review the redline and confirm the VAT/sales tax language and whether additional withholding language is required?

If this is acceptable to Acme, we can issue a final Order Form for signature and route a DocuSign.

Best,
Vanessa

Attachment: orderform_v3_redlines.pdf (application/pdf)

From: aisha_rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-11T16:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form redlines + invoicing questions (legal review)

Vanessa / Ben —

Reviewed the v3 redlines. Quick legal notes to include before signature:

1) Taxes: keep customer-responsible framing. Add a short clause: "Customer shall be responsible for any sales, use, value added, or similar taxes arising from the purchase of Services, except for taxes based on Redwood's net income." That covers our exposure.

2) Withholding: add a one-sentence exception: "If Customer is required by applicable law to withhold taxes, Customer shall provide Redwood with written notice and official documentation; any such withholding shall be reflected on the invoice." Avoids automatic gross-up language.

3) Invoicing address / PO: include a required-field table in the Order Form for PO number and remit-to details; invoices missing a PO will be marked as 'Pending' and we will issue a corrected invoice once PO provided. This reduces AR churn.

4) Minimums and ramp: if we accept $85k, include a true-up clause: "If annual consumption exceeds committed minimum, Customer will be invoiced for overage at the standard per-unit rate; if consumption is below the committed minimum, Customer shall pay the shortfall pro-rata within 30 days of contract anniversary." Keeps accounting clean.

5) Signature mechanics: add a final paragraph referencing DocuSign envelope id and a signature date field.

I will prepare a one-page redline summary for Commercials and send in the morning.

-Aisha
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference
